title: Why does Allah not speak to us? Same words, same hearts.
subtitle: Demanding a private miracle
then: Ibn Abbas said Rafi bin Huraymilah told the Prophet ﷺ: {trap}if you are a messenger, ask Allah to speak to us directly.{/trap} Others said the Arab idolaters said it. Either way, people before them said the same. {idea}Their hearts are alike.{/idea} The signs are already clear for those with certainty.
now: If Allah wants me to pray, He will send me a sign. If this is the right path, something will happen to prove it. Meanwhile the Quran sits on the shelf. {idea}The sign you are waiting for is often the one you are not reading.{/idea}
old: I will commit when Allah gives me a clear sign.
new: The signs are already made plain. Certainty grows by engaging with them.
try: Instead of waiting for a sign today, read one page of the Quran and look for one.

title: Sent with the truth to give good news and warn.
subtitle: The messenger's job, and its limit
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ he was sent {reward}with the truth, a bringer of good news and a warner.{/reward} Ibn Kathir: you will not be asked why others rejected you. Abdullah bin Amr said the Torah described him too: {idea}not harsh, not loud in the markets, forgiving and pardoning.{/idea}
now: Your brother stopped praying. Your friend mocks religion. You lie awake as if their choices were your exam. {idea}Your job is to show and tell, kindly.{/idea} The reckoning is Allah's, not yours.
old: If they do not change, I have failed.
new: My part is to convey with kindness. Their hearts are in Allah's hands.
try: Share one good thing about your faith with someone today, gently, then let it go.

title: Their approval has a price. Allah's guidance is the guidance.
subtitle: Chasing approval at the cost of truth
then: Ibn Jarir explained: {trap}they will never be pleased with you until you follow their way,{/trap} so do not chase what pleases them, but hold to what pleases Allah. The Prophet ﷺ was told to say: {idea}the guidance of Allah is the guidance.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says the warning applies to the whole Ummah.
now: You water down your values to fit in at the office party. You drop a prayer so the group is not uncomfortable. You keep adjusting, and they keep wanting more. {idea}Some approval only comes at the price of yourself.{/idea}
old: If I bend a little more, they will finally accept me.
new: I seek Allah's pleasure first. Approval that costs my guidance is not worth it.
try: Next time you feel pressure to hide your faith to fit in, keep one small practice openly.

title: Recite the Book as it deserves: live what it says.
subtitle: What true recitation means
then: Ibn Masud said true recitation is {idea}to allow what it allows, forbid what it forbids, and not twist its meaning.{/idea} Umar said: when they read a verse of mercy they ask for it, and at a verse of punishment they seek refuge. {reward}The Prophet ﷺ himself did this.{/reward}
now: You finish a juz on your commute with earbuds in, racing the next stop. Try one verse instead. When it mentions mercy, whisper: O Allah, give me that. When it warns, say: protect me. {idea}Reciting becomes talking with Him.{/idea}
old: Reading the Quran means getting through as many pages as I can.
new: Reciting it truly means responding to it and living by it.
try: Read five verses today. Pause at each mercy or warning and respond with a short dua.

title: Remember My favour on you. A blessing is a responsibility.
subtitle: Gifts given, then the question of gratitude
then: This call repeats one from the start of the surah. Ibn Kathir says it is repeated to stress following the Prophet ﷺ described in their books. {reward}Allah reminds them of His favours{/reward} and warns them: {trap}do not let envy of what others were given push you to deny the truth.{/trap}
now: You were born into a Muslim family, taught to pray, given a mosque nearby. It is easy to treat that as status. {idea}A blessing is a question: what will you do with it?{/idea}
old: I was given faith, so I am already ahead.
new: Every favour from Allah is a trust that asks for gratitude and action.
try: List three blessings in your faith life that you did not earn. Thank Allah for each one.

title: A Day when no one can stand in for you.
subtitle: Every soul carries its own load
then: Right after reminding them of favours, the verse turns to the Day of Judgement, echoing the warning from earlier in the surah. {trap}No soul will help another, no compensation will be taken, no intercession will benefit, no one will be helped.{/trap} {idea}Favours in this life do not carry over by themselves.{/idea}
now: In the exam hall, your parents cannot sit the paper for you. In the job interview, your cousin's connections stop at the door. {idea}On that Day, it is you and what you did.{/idea} That is sobering, and it is also in your hands today.
old: My family and community will carry me through.
new: On that Day I stand alone with my deeds, so I prepare now.
try: Do one deed today purely for your own account with Allah, not for anyone watching.

title: Ibrahim passed his tests and became a leader for people.
subtitle: Leadership is earned, not inherited
then: Allah tested Ibrahim with commands and {idea}he fulfilled them all.{/idea} Ibn Abbas listed some: leaving his people, arguing with the king, patience in the fire, leaving his homeland, being told to sacrifice his son. Allah made him a leader. He asked: and my offspring? {trap}My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers.{/trap}
now: Your father was the imam, so you expect respect. Your family founded the charity, so you expect the chair. {idea}Ibrahim earned his place through tests he passed.{/idea} Your name opens doors; only your conduct keeps you there.
old: My family background gives me a place.
new: Standing with Allah comes from passing my own tests, not from my lineage.
try: Think of the test in front of you right now. Ask Allah to help you fulfil it like Ibrahim.

title: The House: a place to return to, and a place of safety.
subtitle: Purify it for those who worship
then: Allah made the House a place people return to and a place of security. He told Ibrahim and Ismail: {idea}purify My House for those who circle it, stay in it, bow and prostrate.{/idea} Ibn Abbas said: purify it from idols. Mujahid added false witness and sins. {reward}The Prophet ﷺ said mosques are for what they were built for.{/reward}
now: Your local mosque: the shoes piled at the door, the bathroom no one cleans, the loud phone call in the prayer hall. {idea}Keeping Allah's house clean and calm is part of Ibrahim's work.{/idea}
old: Cleaning the mosque is the caretaker's job.
new: Purifying Allah's house for worshippers is a task He gave to prophets.
try: At your next visit to the mosque, tidy something small: shoes, books, a spill.

title: Ibrahim prayed for a safe city with fruits for the believers.
subtitle: Allah's provision is wider than our asking

row.title: if I am provided, Allah is pleased
provision is for all; the end differs

then: Ibrahim prayed: {idea}make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits, those who believe.{/idea} Allah answered that He would also give the disbeliever enjoyment for a little while, {trap}then the Fire.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ said Ibrahim made the House sacred and secure, as he made Madinah sacred.
now: Your salary arrives whether you prayed this week or not. The fridge is full either way. {idea}Provision in this world is not a certificate of Allah's pleasure.{/idea} It is a short loan; what matters is where it leads.
old: Things are going well, so Allah must be pleased with me.
new: Allah provides for everyone here. His pleasure is shown by faith and its end.
try: When you next receive money or good food, say alhamdulillah and ask Allah to make it lead you to Him.

title: Building Allah's House, they still asked: accept it from us.
subtitle: The greatest work, with the humblest prayer
then: Ibrahim and his son Ismail raised the foundations of the House with their own hands. {idea}They were doing one of the greatest deeds ever,{/idea} and their words were not pride but a plea: {reward}Our Lord, accept this from us. You are the Hearing, the Knowing.{/reward}
now: You finished organising the iftar, the fundraiser, the Quran class. People thank you. A small voice says: I did well. {idea}Ibrahim's voice says: Lord, accept it.{/idea} Your big deeds need that prayer most.
old: I did a big good deed, so it surely counts.
new: Even the best deed needs Allah's acceptance, so I ask for it humbly.
try: After your next good deed, say Rabbana taqabbal minna, Our Lord accept from us.

title: Make us submit to You, and our children after us.
subtitle: A prophet still asking to be a Muslim
then: While building the House, Ibrahim and Ismail kept praying. {idea}Make us submit to You, and make our descendants a nation that submits.{/idea} They asked to be shown how to worship and {reward}for their repentance to be accepted{/reward}, though they were prophets doing Allah's work.
now: You worry about your children's faith, scrolling articles at midnight. Ibrahim's way: keep asking Allah for them, and for yourself first. {idea}A prophet asked to be made a Muslim. You can ask too.{/idea}
old: I am already a Muslim, so I do not need to ask for it.
new: Staying submitted to Allah is a gift I ask for daily, for me and my children.
try: Make this dua today for yourself and your family: Our Lord, make us submit to You.

title: Ibrahim prayed for a messenger. The answer was Muhammad ﷺ.
subtitle: A dua answered centuries later
then: Ibrahim asked Allah to {idea}send among them a messenger from themselves{/idea} to recite, teach the Book and wisdom, and purify them. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said wisdom is the Sunnah. The Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}I am the dua of my father Ibrahim and the good news of Isa.{/reward}
now: You prayed for years for something and it has not come. Ibrahim never saw his answer in his lifetime. {reward}It came, and it changed the world.{/reward} Your dua for your grandchildren may still be working long after you.
old: If my dua is not answered soon, it is not going to be.
new: Allah answers in His time. Some answers outlive the one who asked.
try: Make one dua today for people who will come after you: your children, students, or community.
